# Introduction

This vignette demonstrates how to use the package 'slate'. Very simplified data can be simulated for demonstration using simulation function provided in the package.

```{r setup}
library(slate)
```

## Simulate example data

For this example, the data is Y (nxp matrix of features), a covariate for survival, and survival time and event status. A matrix Zt for the design of the p features is included, with indicators for group membership of the features.

```{r simulate}
set.seed(3302)
sim_data <- slate_sim_test_data()

str(sim_data)
```



## Fit slate model with specifed alpha and lambda penalty parameters

```{r fit_slate} 
fit <- slate(Y=sim_data$Y, Zt=sim_data$Zt, surv_covar=sim_data$surv_covar,
            surv_time=sim_data$surv_time, 
            surv_event=sim_data$surv_event, alpha=.5, lambda=1.2)

summary(fit)
```


## Fit a grid of slate models over alpha and lambda penalty parameters

Note that the range of lambda depends on input data, so we create a vector of
fractions that govern the lambda used. The maximum lambda forces all W loadings to 0, so we create a vector that begins with the largest lambda and subsequently reduce the lamda
according to the fraction of the maximum lambda. Alpha grid ranges from 1 to a small value greater than 0.

```{r fit_grid}

alpha_grid <- c((10:1)/10)
nlambda <- 10
lambda_frac <- exp(seq(log(1),
                       log(.1),
                       length.out = nlambda))

fit_grid <- slate_grid(Y=sim_data$Y, Zt=sim_data$Zt, surv_covar=sim_data$surv_covar,
                      surv_time=sim_data$surv_time, 
                      surv_event=sim_data$surv_event,  
                      alpha_grid, lambda_frac, maxiter=50)
names(fit_grid)
dim(fit_grid$grid)

```

## Find best fitting model over grid determined by minimum bic

```{r best_fit}

fit_best <- slate_best_fit(fit_grid)
summary(fit_best)

```
